items.title: Buddy Burton Interview, 1959-09-07
items.q: INTERVIEWER: Elliot? [INTERVIEWEE] Elliot Washington. Elliot Washington.

ctx.x: I get up there, and here was it. One of the men dropped out on us, and Melrose says, oh, Burton says, he used to always use me to sort of this side kick, you know, along those lines, your trouble come up, and I says, well, I know a fellow here in Harlem that is a good saxophone player and a clarinet player that used to play with Ma Rainey, and he's here. And I says, I'm sure, and he made so many records with Ma Rainey, I says, he'll fit right into the picture because he knows how to handle himself and the tones…
and lives right across the street here. Oh, he's here in town now. Yeah, yeah, I seen him yesterday from a distance. Elliot?

Elliot Washington. Elliot Washington. And so I says, yeah, I says, now I'll give you a number, you go down and see about him and get him and tell him I'm here and that we want him to go out and I say to so-and-so, and he'll listen to you and he'll come with you. Now, I'll take the two men down to the recording studio, which Big Bill is playing guitar and singing some blues.
